subtopic: Menstrual cycle effects on mood and coping
passage:
Coach's note, college hockey squad, for my own records.
Swati, our right half, showed me her phone today. She has been tracking her cycle alongside her training log for months and has noticed that a few days each month she feels heavier, teary and slower off the mark, while the following week she feels unstoppable. She was worried I would see it as weakness. I told her it is the opposite: it is information about her own body. We agreed that on her low-energy days she will do skills drills and lighter conditioning, and push hard on her strong days. She will tell me with one word, "green" or "amber", so she needn't explain in front of the team. I will check in next month on how it is working.
Suraj

qa.q: What one-word signals will Swati use?
What was Swati worried about when she showed the coach her phone?
qa.a: She was anxious that Suraj would see her low days as weakness.

qa.q: Why is the plan a wise one?
qa.a: It uses Swati's own pattern to plan lighter drills on low days and hard training on strong days, without treating her as weak.

qa.q: How does Suraj see Swati's tracking?
qa.a: Suraj sees it as useful information about her own body, not a weakness, and adjusts training to match.

grounding: Shows a young woman tracking her cycle, spotting lower-energy and stronger days, and planning lighter work without treating it as weakness.

passage:
Tuesday night
Cried at a dog food advert today. Actually cried. Then snapped at Dilnaz for leaving her mug on my desk, and felt awful. When I opened my cycle tracker to log it, there it was again: the same few days every month when I'm low, teary and everything feels too loud. A week later I'm the girl who volunteers for every presentation. Seeing the pattern on the screen made me feel less crazy. It isn't weakness; it's just my rhythm. So next month I'm not booking the debate trials on those days. Early nights, lighter reading, a long walk. I told Dilnaz and said sorry about the mug. She said she's noticed her own low days too, and we're going to compare notes. Weirdly comforting.
Mahima

qa.q: How did Mahima feel after seeing the pattern in the tracker?
qa.a: She felt relieved and less crazy, seeing it as her rhythm rather than weakness.

qa.q: How does Mahima plan to use what she learned?
qa.a: By not booking debate trials on the low days and planning early nights, lighter reading and a walk instead.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz feel about Mahima's apology and explanation?
qa.a: She seems understanding and even glad, since she has noticed her own low days and wants to compare notes.

grounding: Illustrates a young woman noticing through tracking that some days bring tearfulness and low energy, and planning rest without seeing it as weakness.
